extracted.intended_audience: F99/K00 fellowship review committee members and fellowship selection committee
extracted.subtask_description: Sponsor and co-sponsor statements and training plan for an NIH F99/K00 fellowship applicant describing training goals, mentorship commitments, institutional resources, and evidence of the applicant's qualifications and readiness for an independent research career.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integration of qualitative and quantitative findings
rubrics_metrics.description: (b) integration of qualitative and quantitative findings
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ms. Yu proposes a mixed-methods dissertation and will be trained to build knowledge with both longitudinal survey data and qualitative perspectives; Dr. Palinkas will work with Ms. Yu to formulate purposeful sampling, data collection, and analysis plans and to prepare manuscripts reporting mixed-methods study findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Developing/adapting interventions with target group and community organizations
rubrics_metrics.description: (c) developing and/or adapting social isolation and cognitive health intervention in collaboration with the target age group and community-based organizations
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ms. Yu has prior co-design experience (CSMP app) and will continue community-based intervention conceptualization and co-design with mentors; will participate in pilot qualitative focus groups and collaborate with community partners to adapt IMTOP and other interventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific writing and navigating the peer-review process
rubrics_metrics.description: (d) scientific writing and navigating the peer-review process
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mentors will provide manuscript collaboration opportunities, feedback in journal club presentations, and guidance on grant and manuscript preparation; Ms. Yu will collaborate on manuscripts and receive feedback from peers and mentors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Increase knowledge in prevention, intervention, practice, and policy for cognitive decline/ADRD
rubrics_metrics.description: Training Goal 1: Ms. Yu will increase knowledge in prevention, intervention, and current practice and policy pertain[ing to] cognitive decline in normal aging and the development of ADRD.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Activities include connections with USC ADRC researchers, developing a literature review database, presenting at a bi-weekly journal club, involvement with USC ADRC and OADC investigator meetings, attending ADRD-related conferences (AAIC, GSA, CTAD), and monthly meetings with senior mentors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Active engagement in scholarly communities and presentation skills
rubrics_metrics.description: Present learned ADRD-related knowledge in journal club and at conferences; receive interactive feedback
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At the bi-weekly journal club Ms. Yu will present, engage in discussions, and receive feedback from peers and mentors to formulate an intellectual community and academic support system that advances professional development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regular, structured mentorship and access to senior scientists
rubrics_metrics.description: Frequent mentor interactions and availability of sponsors/co-sponsors for methodological and substantive guidance
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit commitments: meet with Dr. Dodge at least once a month during F99 phase; monthly consultations with Dr. Palinkas; weekly mentoring meetings with Dr. Wu and the primary sponsor; sponsors/co-sponsors to meet in-person once a year at major scientific meetings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training in analyzing high-frequency digital biomarker longitudinal data and neuroimaging methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Training Goal 2: Ms. Yu will gain skills in analyzing high-frequency digital biomarkers longitudinal data and employing neuroimaging methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Planned activities include bi-weekly directed readings on example studies, presenting learning outcomes in regular meetings, seminars and training at OADC neuroimaging and biomarker cores, hands-on work with I-CONECT data, and supervised self-directed learning of R programming to manage longitudinal biomarker data; Dr. Dodge will connect Ms. Yu with specialists and supervise methodology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advanced training in design, implementation, and evaluation of community-based interventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Training Goal 3: Ms. Yu will receive advanced training on design, implement[ation], and evaluate community-based interventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mentoring includes guidance on conceptualizing intervention studies, weekly discussions of practical/intervention/policy implications, immersion with I-CONECT fieldwork, taking an online UCSF course on study design for intervention research, and applying to a NINDS clinical trial methodology course (R25) for sustained training in trial protocol development and grant planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immersion in fieldwork and practical trial implementation processes
rubrics_metrics.description: Immersion training with I-CONECT fieldwork to observe recruitment, enrollment, and randomization processes
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ms. Yu will observe team monitoring of trial processes, attend investigator meetings (monthly OADC investigator meetings and K00 in-person), and receive hands-on experience relevant to practical clinical trial conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to institutional resources, research cores, and facilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Environment and Research Facilities: access to USC Hamovitch Center, USC ADRC, OADC, and their research cores
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed Facilities and Other Resources describe available cores; in K00 phase Ms. Yu will attend trainings and seminars hosted by neuroimaging and biomarker cores and be directed to other research cores as needed to meet learning and research needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mentor team composition and adequate mentoring capacity
rubrics_metrics.description: Experienced and committed sponsor/co-sponsor team to contribute to professional development and facilitate transition to independent scientist
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PI coordinates communication among co-sponsors; the application lists other fellows/trainees supervised by mentors (names and roles) to demonstrate mentors have time/resources to support Ms. Yu's dissertation and postdoctoral research; co-sponsors will meet yearly in-person.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence of applicant qualifications and potential for an independent research career
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant’s qualifications and Potential for a Research Career: prior research experience, publications, presentations, awards, and demonstrated methodological sophistication and independence
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific evidence provided: two years as research assistant, systematic review publication, first-authored 12 conference presentations, high-quality manuscripts, APHA Nobuo Maeda International Research Award, first-authored papers under revise-and-resubmit, experience with longitudinal datasets (HRS, NHATS) and advanced analytic methods (random intercept cross-lagged modeling), leadership in pilot studies, and experience supervising student workers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of nationally representative longitudinal datasets for rigorous causal inference
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of NHATS (4 waves) and HRS longitudinal data to investigate living environment effects on social isolation and cognition
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proposal emphasizes national representative longitudinal data to draw more rigorous conclusions regarding hypothesized causal effects; planned longitudinal analyses bridge interests in physical health and social isolation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training and competence in statistical/methodological tools and programming
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop methodological skills including R programming and advanced statistical methods for longitudinal and biomarker data
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dr. Dodge will supervise self-directed R programming learning for managing high-frequency longitudinal biomarker data; mentorship will connect Ms. Yu to neuroimaging and biomarker analysis experts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissemination and professional networking through conferences and presentations
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit abstracts and present at cognitive health-related conferences (AAIC, GSA, CTAD) to expand academic network and disseminate findings
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participation in conferences is part of the training plan to enhance visibility, feedback, and professional development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Development of grant-writing and pilot-study preparation skills
rubrics_metrics.description: Preparation to apply for pilot grants and develop intervention research proposals
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mentors will collaborate on pilot qualitative studies, guide drafting of intervention proposals, and provide training in grant preparation (including R25 clinical trial methodology course) to prepare Ms. Yu for independent funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community-engaged recruitment, data collection, and co-design experience
rubrics_metrics.description: Experience and training in recruitment, semi-structured interview design, qualitative data collection and co-design with community partners
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ms. Yu's prior roles include recruiting older adults, demonstrating mobile apps, conducting interviews, leading qualitative data analysis, and supervising community recruitment; these experiences are explicitly leveraged to train in community-based intervention research.
